photos.title: Myrtle Beach oceanfront, houses and condo towers side by side, USGS oblique aerial photo, August 24, 2011
photos.what: The Myrtle Beach oceanfront seen from a plane over the ocean: on the left, older two-story houses on lawns between the beach and Ocean Boulevard, with streets of houses under oaks behind them; on the right, two condo and hotel towers on the beach.
photos.caption: Houses and condo towers on the beach in Myrtle Beach, with wooden walkways over the dunes to the sand.
photos.alt: Older two-story houses on lawns along the beach at left, and two tall condo towers on the beach at right, with streets of houses under oak trees behind, seen from a plane over the ocean in Myrtle Beach
photos.author: U.S. Geological Survey
photos.credit: Photo: U.S. Geological Survey, public domain. Credit not required; give it anyway.
photos.provenance: U.S. government photo: USGS baseline coastal oblique aerial survey 11CCH03 (Ponte Vedra, Florida, to the South Carolina/North Carolina border), flown 2011-08-24, photographer Karen L.M. Morgan (USGS). Frame 2011_0824_180143d.jpg from https://coastal.er.usgs.gov/data-release/doi-F7N877XX/data/11CCH03_0824_180000.zip; aircraft position 33.718773 N, -78.838295 W (11CCH03-Photolocations.csv and the file's EXIF GPS; the position of the plane, not of the buildings). Data release: Morgan, K.L.M., 2017, https://doi.org/10.5066/F7N877XX. Not the frame used on any other page (other pages use 174830, 175156, 175537, 180052, 180608 and 181208).

photos.subject_check: Looked at full size (3008 px, in two halves) by the writer of /submarkets/myrtle-beach/ on 2026-11-02. Placed by testing points 500 to 600 m inland of the plane's position, 250 m either side, against map-str-zones.geojson: R zone at the left and the middle, shaded (nightly rentals) at the right, which matches houses at left and towers at right. People on the beach are too small to recognize; no readable sign, logo, plate or house number at page size.
